turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_fatigue_train.csv: 293 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si,
    Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and `target` (the
    measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).
  - b3_fatigue_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose rotating-bending
    fatigue strength (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the
    same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST rotating-
bending fatigue strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**1. Process family dominates.** The training set splits into clear process families with very different fatigue strength levels:

| Family (key signature) | typical target |
|---|---|
| Normalized only (NT 885, no THT/TT) | 232–275 |
| Through-hardened + temper 550–650 °C (Q&T, plain/low-alloy) | 325–540 |
| Q&T with ~1 % Cr / Cr–Mo / Ni–Cr–Mo | 460–645 |
| Q&T high-Si (1.3–2.0 % Si) spring steels, temper 420–500 °C | 678–906 |
| **Carburized (CT = 930, Ct = 90–540 min, DT ≈ 850–900, low temper TT = 160–200 °C)** | **838–1144** |

So the carburized rows (case-hardened, ~0.2 % core C, tempered at only 160–200 °C) are in a class of their own — mean ≈ 990, max = 1144. Any candidate from that family beats every Q&T candidate.

**2. Within the carburized family**, secondary trends:
- Longer carburizing time Ct (≈340–500 min) and longer diffusion Dt (≈35–70 min) → higher strength than short Ct (90–140 min).
- TT 160 °C slightly better than 200 °C (~20–40 MPa).
- Alloying helps: high Cr (~1.1 %) with Mo ~0.17, or Ni ~1.6, or Ni–Cr–Mo, give the top numbers (1074–1144). The 0.20 C/0.46 Ni/0.47 Cr grade is the weakest of the group (~930–960).

**3. Pool screening.** Carburized candidates: c000, c016, c018, c046, c050, c053, c054, c062, c063, c075, c081. Estimated by nearest-neighbour/analog matching:

- **c081** – 0.21 C, 1.17 Cr, 0.17 Mo, Ct 340.2, Dt 70.2, QmT 60, TT 200. Identical material/process to the 1144 MPa record (only TT 200 vs 160) → ≈ 1110. **Best.**
- **c053** – 0.23 C, 1.69 Ni, 0.55 Cr, 0.18 Mo (the grade that gave 1110 MPa), TT 160 → ≈ 1080.
- **c016** – 0.17 C, 1.64 Ni grade with Ct 469.8 process that gave 1082 MPa (TT 200) → ≈ 1065.
- **c063** – 0.21 C, 1.62 Ni, 0.21 Mo, Ct 469.8, TT 160 (analogs 1034–1054) → ≈ 1050.
- **c062 / c018** – same Ni grades, shorter Ct or higher TT → ≈ 1030–1040.
- c046/c054/c000 ≈ 1000–1030; c050/c075 (0.46 Ni/0.47 Cr grade) ≈ 930–960.

Non-carburized best-in-pool (c094 high-Si 2.05 %, c019, c052 ≈ 790–860) fall clearly below the carburized group, so none make the top 5.

**Final: c081, c053, c016, c063, c062**
